question: When are SASSA payments made in 2026?
answer:

  • Old Age Grants: 2nd-3rd of each month
  • Disability Grants: 4th-5th of each month
  • Child Support Grants: Starting from the 6th of each month
  • Foster Care & Care Dependency Grants: Mid-month, typically 10th-15th

question: How do I apply for a SASSA grant in 2026?
answer:
Applying for a SASSA grant is straightforward but requires preparation. Follow these steps:

  1. Visit a SASSA office or outreach event – Locate one via our resources page.
  2. Gather documents:
    • South African ID
    • Proof of income (if any)
    • 3-month bank statements
    • Medical reports (for Disability Grant)
    • Child’s birth certificate (for Child Support or Foster Care Grants)
  3. Fill out the application form with SASSA staff assistance.
  4. Submit and get a receipt – Keep it safe!
  5. Wait for processing – Typically 30-90 days, depending on the grant type.

Online Option (for SRD Grant): Apply via srd.sassa.gov.za using your ID and mobile number.

Warning: SASSA applications are FREE. Avoid scams by applying only through official channels. Learn more about fraud prevention on our scam alerts page.

question: What should I do if my SASSA card is lost or stolen?
answer:
If your SASSA card is lost or stolen, act quickly to protect your funds:

Immediate Steps:

  1. Report to Police: Obtain a case number for theft/loss
  2. Contact SASSA: Call 0800 60 10 11 or visit a SASSA office to block the card
  3. Request Replacement: Apply for a new card at a SASSA office

Documents Needed:

  • South African ID
  • Police case number (for theft)
  • Affidavit for loss

Replacement Process:

  • Complete a lost/stolen card form
  • Pay a small fee (if applicable)
  • Wait 7-14 days for the new card
  • Collect at your designated pay point

Good News: You can still collect grants with your ID at pay points while waiting. Stay safe with our fraud prevention tips.

question: What does it mean when my SASSA application status says 'Pending', 'Approved', or 'Declined'?
answer:
Pending means SASSA is still verifying your details against government databases this month. Approved means you qualify for that month and a pay date will appear once assigned. Declined means a rule was not met for that month, and the reason is shown on your status page.

Statuses like Referred, Bank Details Pending, Cancelled, Suspended and Failed each have a specific meaning and next step.

question: How do I join a SASSA WhatsApp group for updates in 2026?
answer: SASSA does not run public WhatsApp groups. Any group claiming to be an official SASSA group, or asking for your OTP, PIN or banking details, is a scam.

question: Why is my SASSA SRD grant still pending after weeks?
answer:
A status that stays Pending for weeks usually means one of the checks has not cleared: bank-account verification, an identity or eKYC/biometric check, or a match against UIF, SARS or another grant.

Check that your banking details are active and in your own name, complete any enrolment SASSA asked for, and avoid resubmitting repeatedly. If nothing changes after two to three weeks, call SASSA on 0800 60 10 11.

question: What is the SASSA mandatory biometric system (since September 2025)?
answer: SASSA's mandatory biometric (facial) verification, rolled out for SRD applicants since 2025, confirms that the person applying is the person linked to the ID number. You complete it through the official SRD portal or the SASSA app by following the selfie/enrolment prompt sent to you.

question: Who needs to complete the SASSA biometric enrolment?
answer:
Since 1 September 2025, the mandatory biometric enrolment applies to:

  • New Applicants: Anyone applying for a SASSA grant (e.g., Child Support, Disability, SRD) must provide fingerprints or facial recognition data.
  • Existing Beneficiaries Under Review: Those flagged for identity checks or updating personal details may need to enroll.
  • Alternative ID Users: Beneficiaries using non-standard IDs (e.g., refugee and asylum seeker permits) must comply.

Exemption: Current beneficiaries not under review are not required to enroll immediately but may need to later. Bring your South African ID to a SASSA office for a quick scan. Check our biometrics guide or call 0800 60 10 11 for clarification.

question: How do I complete the SASSA biometric enrolment process in 2026?
answer:
To complete the mandatory biometric enrolment since 1 September 2025:

  1. Visit a SASSA Office: Go to your nearest SASSA branch or mobile unit.
  2. Bring Documents: Carry your South African ID (smart ID preferred), or alternative IDs like green ID book or Home Affairs receipts.
  3. Biometric Capture: Staff will scan your fingerprints or face using electronic Know Your Client (eKYC) technology. The process takes minutes.
  4. Receive Confirmation: Get a reference number to track your application.

Important: Applications without biometrics will be flagged for review, delaying payments. Visit www.sassa.gov.za or check our biometrics guide for office locations and tips.

question: What happens if I don’t complete the SASSA biometric enrolment in 2026?
answer:
If you fail to complete the mandatory biometric enrolment (which has applied since 1 September 2025):

  • New Applicants: Your grant application will be placed under review and not processed until biometrics are captured.
  • Existing Beneficiaries: If flagged for review (e.g., due to alternative IDs or suspicious activity), your grant may be suspended until you comply.
  • Deadline Risks: Missing a deadline set by SASSA can lead to grant suspension until you complete the process.

Action: Visit a SASSA office with your ID to enroll. Check notifications via SMS or srd.sassa.gov.za. See our biometrics guide for details.

question: Will elderly SASSA beneficiaries need to provide biometrics in 2026?
answer:
Elderly SASSA beneficiaries (60+ years, receiving Old Age Grants) are not immediately required to provide biometrics unless they are:

  • New Applicants: Applying for a grant after 1 September 2025.
  • Flagged for Review: Due to alternative IDs, data updates, or suspected fraud.
  • Updating Details: Changing payment methods or personal information.

Concerns: Some elderly beneficiaries worry about unreadable fingerprints due to age. SASSA offers facial recognition as an alternative. For mobility issues, contact 0800 60 1011 to arrange assistance or mobile unit visits. Check our biometrics guide for support options.

question: How does the SASSA biometric system prevent fraud in 2026?
answer:
The SASSA biometric system, mandatory from 1 September 2025, prevents fraud by:

  • Verifying Identity: Fingerprints and facial recognition ensure applicants are authentic and alive.
  • Reducing Duplicates: Detects multiple applications using the same ID.
  • Stopping Forgery: Replaces unreliable green ID checks with secure eKYC technology.
  • Flagging Issues: Applications without biometrics are reviewed, preventing unauthorized payments.

Impact: Identity theft attempts and payments made against deceased beneficiaries have been reported in past years, highlighting the need for this system. Learn more on our fraud prevention page or visit www.sassa.gov.za.

  • Data Mismatch: Details don’t match Home Affairs records.

Notification: SASSA will send an SMS or letter. Check status at srd.sassa.gov.za or SMS your ID to 34548 (R1). Visit our tracking guide.

question: Can I use a smart ID for SASSA biometric enrolment in 2026?
answer:
Yes, a smart ID is preferred for SASSA biometric enrolment since 1 September 2025. It aligns with the electronic Know Your Client (eKYC) system for faster verification. Other acceptable IDs include:

  • Green ID book
  • Home Affairs receipts
  • Refugee/asylum seeker permits

Tip: Ensure your ID is valid and matches Home Affairs records. Visit a SASSA office for enrolment. Check our biometrics guide or call 0800 60 10 11 for assistance.

question: Why did SASSA pay grants to deceased beneficiaries?
answer:
In past years SASSA has acknowledged payments being made against the records of deceased beneficiaries due to system vulnerabilities, such as:

  • Weak Verification: Lack of biometric checks before September 2025.
  • Fraudulent Claims: Forged IDs or unreported deaths.
  • System Delays: Slow updates from Home Affairs records.

Solution: The mandatory biometric system since September 2025 ensures proof of life. Report suspected fraud to fraud@sassa.gov.za. Visit our fraud prevention page.

question: How do I update my SASSA payment method to a bank account in 2026?
answer:
To update your SASSA payment method to a bank account in 2026:

  1. Visit a SASSA Office: Bring your ID and bank confirmation letter (not older than 3 months).
  2. Complete Form: Fill out the payment method change form.
  3. Biometric Verification: Since September 2025, provide fingerprints or facial scans.
  4. Wait for Processing: Takes 1-2 months; check status via 0800 60 10 11.

Tip: Ensure bank details match your ID. Visit our payment guide.

question: How do I contact SASSA for urgent issues in 2026?
answer:
For urgent SASSA issues in 2026 (e.g., delayed payments, suspensions):

Contact Options:

  • Toll-Free: 0800 60 10 11 (Mon-Fri, 8 AM-4 PM)

question: Can I collect my SASSA grant at a retailer like Checkers in 2026?
answer:
Yes, you can collect your SASSA grant at retailers like Checkers, Shoprite, or Pick n Pay in 2026 if you use a SASSA card or cash paypoint.

Steps:

  1. Bring your South African ID and SASSA card.
  2. Verify identity (biometrics may be required since September 2025).
  3. Collect funds at the till or designated counter.

Note: Check payment schedules at www.sassa.gov.za. Visit our payment guide for retailer locations.

question: What should I do if I receive a suspicious SASSA SMS in 2026?
answer:
Suspicious SASSA SMS messages may be scams. Take these steps:

  1. Don’t Click Links: Avoid links not from srd.sassa.gov.za or www.sassa.gov.za.
  2. Verify Source: Official SASSA SMS comes from verified numbers or includes your reference number.
  3. Report: Forward the SMS to 0800 60 10 11 or email fraud@sassa.gov.za.
  4. Protect Data: Never share ID, PIN, or bank details.

Tip: Check our fraud prevention page for scam examples and safety tips.

question: What does 'Referred' status mean for SASSA SRD in 2026?
answer: 'Referred' status means your application was flagged during the automated cross-check with internal or external databases (like SARS or Home Affairs). It requires a manual review by a SASSA official to verify that you meet the income threshold or citizenship requirements.

question: Why is my SASSA status 'Bank Details Pending' for months?
answer: This usually happens because you haven't selected a payment method or the banking details provided did not pass the verification test. Ensure the account belongs to you and is a personal, active account. Log in to the SRD portal to re-submit your details if necessary.

question: I received an SMS about a SASSA grant review — is it real?
answer: Genuine SASSA review SMS messages come from registered short codes (not regular cellphone numbers or WhatsApp). They tell you to visit a SASSA office and list the documents you need to bring. They never ask for your PIN, OTP, or banking password. If the message contains a clickable link, demands payment, or creates false urgency, it is a scam. When in doubt, call the SASSA helpline on 0800 60 10 11 to verify. For detailed guidance, see our guide on what to do if SASSA asks you to update your information.

question: What documents do I need for a SASSA grant review appointment?
answer: For a grant review appointment, bring: your original South African ID (or alternative ID document), proof of residence dated within 3 months, your SASSA card if you have one, proof of income (payslips, bank statements, or an affidavit if unemployed), and any documents SASSA specifically requested in their SMS or letter. Bring originals plus photocopies. For a full walkthrough, see our grant review and verification guide.

question: Why is the SASSA SRD status check not loading today?
answer: The SRD portal is often slow or down at month-end when millions check at once, or during maintenance. Wait two to four hours and retry on a different browser or network. While it is down you can still check via WhatsApp (082 601 0111), USSD (*120*69277#), or the SASSA call centre (0800 60 10 11).

question: How long does it take for my SASSA SRD payment to reflect in my bank account?
answer: Allow two to three business days after your assigned pay date for bank deposits. Cash Send payments usually arrive the same day or the next business day, and Postbank Black Card funds are normally available on the release date. Confirm your personal pay date on your status page first.

question: Do I need to reapply for the SRD grant every month?
answer: No. Most approved applicants are reassessed automatically every month and do not need to reapply. Only apply again if your status says Reapplication Required or your application has lapsed. Never submit a duplicate application while one is active - it can trigger a fraud flag.

question: Is the SRD grant ending or increasing to R400 or R700?
answer: No. The grant remains R370 per month and has been funded until 31 March 2027. No increase was announced. Social media posts claiming the grant is ending immediately, or that a R400/R700 replacement grant is coming, are false. The court appeal over the SRD regulations is still awaiting judgment and nothing has changed yet.

question: How do I change my SASSA SRD phone number?
answer: Update your mobile number in the official SRD portal using the change-details flow. You must be able to receive the OTP/SMS on the new number, and it needs to be the SIM you will use for future status checks and payment messages.

question: My SASSA appeal was declined - is there anything else I can do?
answer: For that specific month, the appeal decision is final within SASSA's system - you cannot submit a second appeal for the same month. Future months are assessed independently, so keep checking your status. If you believe the process was unlawful or unfair, you can pursue judicial review through the courts; Legal Aid South Africa (0800 110 110) offers free advice where you qualify.

linkedPage.label: How to appeal a declined SRD application

question: What does 'Cancelled' or 'Suspended' mean on my SASSA SRD status?
answer: Cancelled means your grant was closed, so you must submit a fresh application for the current cycle. Suspended means payments are paused, usually after a failed identity or biometric check - complete your eKYC enrolment or visit a SASSA office to reactivate it.
